title: LLC annual-compliance penalties, per jurisdiction
description: v2 (2026-08-11, E11) - the pruned consumer-facing contract. Records the late-fee shape for an LLC's recurring periodic obligation, how long delinquency runs before administrative dissolution, and the reinstatement fee after it. Deliberately minimal: one flat amount or one monthly rate, no penalty matrices, no interest tables, no long-form legal reasoning - the fields carry what a state page renders, evidence carries one sentence per value, and everything else lives in git history. This namespace is authoritative for these values.

lateFeeUsd.description: Flat late fee in USD. null when the state uses a rate or publishes none.

lateFeeRatePercentPerMonth.description: Monthly percentage or interest rate. The only rate field, by design: no interest tables, no compounding schedules.

lateFeeBasis.description: What the state actually publishes. mixed means more than one shape applies; the dominant figure goes in the fields and the rest in notes. A none requires the agency's own publication (form, fee schedule, FAQ) as evidence - statute silence alone never grounds it (E12).

reinstatementFeeUsd.description: The fee to reinstate after administrative dissolution, including any per-year component folded in; reinstatementNote says how. Read the agency's reinstatement form and fee schedule before concluding null (E12).

reinstatementNote.description: One short sentence: what reinstatement requires, such as delinquent reports, per-year fees, or a time window.

administrativeDissolutionAfterDays.description: How long a delinquent LLC may stay delinquent before the state may administratively dissolve or revoke it, when the publisher states that interval in days. null when the publisher states it in months, or states none.

administrativeDissolutionAfterMonths.description: The same interval when the publisher states it in months or years (years x 12). At most one of the two fields is populated, and it is the unit the publisher used: converting months to days is inference, not data. notes names what the interval runs from - the due date, a notice, or a second missed report.

notes.description: One to two sentences only: the recurring obligation and its period, plus the single nuance the fields cannot carry without lying (what the dissolution clock runs from, a calendar-date dissolution, the E10 mixed shape). Legal reasoning stays in git history, not here.

needsReview.description: What is missing and what would settle it.

lastVerified.description: The date the cited pages were retrieved and every quoted passage was mechanically confirmed to occur in them.

quote.description: One contiguous verbatim passage carrying the figure or ruling, copied from the page as retrieved, artefacts included. Never assembled across an ellipsis, never taken from a search snippet, never tidied.

supports.description: Which value in the enclosing object this passage grounds, by field name (lateFeeUsd, reinstatementFeeUsd, ...). A record carrying several passages is only honest if each one says what it is evidence for.
